meta.status: PROVISIONAL — assumptions only, no measured data yet (issue #45, 12 October 2026)

maps_to_evaluation_plan.quiet: between semesters; no counterpart load test, lower bound for idle cost
maps_to_evaluation_plan.typical: W1 Steady (2 searches/s for 10 min, warm cache) extrapolated to a month
maps_to_evaluation_plan.bursty: W2 Burst (ramp 1->50 req/s in 60 s, hold 5 min) plus W3 Long tail (cold commute cache)

meta.how_to_refine: Replace any field whose source is 'assumed' with a measured value from #30 (E1/E2) or #34 (E8/E9). Every field is used by model/cost_model.py; nothing is hardcoded in the report text.

fixed_facts.towns_source: docs/backend-design.md + #2 data profile (PR #52): 27 HDB towns in the September 2026 rent source, each represented by one MRT station. 26 are routable; TENGAH's only reference point is the unopened Jurong Region Line (JS3/JS4) and OneMap PT routing returns 404 from it, so its pairs are enqueued and recorded as unavailable rather than skipped.
fixed_facts.ddb_requests_source: docs/api-contract.md access patterns A1+A6+A7 (design budget, to be measured in #30)

quiet.label: Quiet (between semesters)
quiet.notes: Cache is cold-ish because few groups share destinations.

typical.label: Typical (normal term month)
typical.notes: W1 Steady is 2 searches/s for 10 minutes = 1200 searches; a month at that intensity for ~1 h/day would be ~36k searches, far above a student project. 500 groups x 2 searches = 1000 searches/month is the honest prototype figure; the W1 rate is used for latency, not for volume.

bursty.label: Bursty (semester start, W2 peak + W3 cold cache)
bursty.notes: W2 admitted at 50 req/s requires raising the HTTP API stage throttle (currently 20 req/s burst 40) on the eval stage only — D-E1/D-E2. Cache hit falls because destinations are long-tail at semester start (W3).

shared_assumptions.distinct_member_stations_source: assumed = members_per_group; api-contract A7 caps commute queries at 5 per search
shared_assumptions.lambda_api_duration_source: assumed — MUST be replaced by #30 (E1) CloudWatch Lambda duration
shared_assumptions.lambda_worker_duration_source: assumed — one OneMap routing call per job; replace with #15/#27 worker metrics
shared_assumptions.lambda_worker_routing_latency_source: measured 2026-10-20 through the deployed module from outside Singapore (docs/evaluation/worker-routing/: uncached p50 992 ms, n=8; a cached repeat of the same pairs was 154 ms). This is the routing call alone, not the whole invocation, so lambda_worker_duration_ms still needs CloudWatch from #27.
shared_assumptions.cold_start_share_source: assumed — #30 (E1) reports cold-start share and init duration
shared_assumptions.log_bytes_source: assumed for Powertools structured JSON at INFO; replace with CloudWatch IncomingBytes from #34
shared_assumptions.ddb_rru_source: assumed: eventually-consistent reads of a few small items (0.5 RRU per 4 KB). Replace with ConsumedReadCapacityUnits from #34
shared_assumptions.ddb_wru_source: assumed: 1 WRU per 1 KB item, transactional joins cost 2x. Replace with ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits from #34
shared_assumptions.onemap_calls_per_job_source: #15 worker: one routing call per delivery, and numItineraries=3 is still one call. A job is delivered again only on a transient failure, so the worst case is COMMUTE_MAX_RECEIVES = 3 calls for a job that keeps being throttled, while a terminal failure (404, invalid request) spends exactly one.
shared_assumptions.sqs_idle_poll_source: assumed: Lambda event-source mapping keeps ~5 long-polling consumers at 20 s waits (~130k receives each). VERIFY in #34 against the SQS request count in Cost Explorer — this is the one line item that is not zero when nobody uses the app
shared_assumptions.cloudwatch_source: docs/backend-design.md evaluation hooks: Powertools metrics, SQS age and DLQ alarms
